core_obligations: Reduce to the case of an algebraically closed or larger base field, take an irreducible component Z of the complement of W of positive dimension, and produce a point of Z after base change with at least one coordinate transcendental over the prime field (proof lines 7863-7872).
In characteristic zero, show that the translation operators T_{i,j,0} already move the point through all nonnegative lattice translates, so the orbit is dense (proof lines 7875-7881).

In characteristic p, choose a transcendental coordinate and use the operators T_{i,n,d} to realise all polynomial translates of the remaining coordinates by polynomials in that coordinate; conclude that the closure contains a coordinate hyperplane, then repeat with another coordinate to get infinitely many translates and hence density (proof lines 7882-7895).
Dispose of the zero dimensional case with the same argument and conclude the statement for the complement of W (proof lines 7897-7900).
proof_roadmap: Reduction and the density claim (proof lines 7863-7872).
Characteristic zero case by translations (proof lines 7875-7881).
Characteristic p case by polynomial translates (proof lines 7882-7895).
difficulty_reason: For a field k, n at least 2, and the elementary automorphisms T_{i,j,d} of affine n-space sending x_i to x_i + x_j^d, the lemma describes the nonempty open subschemes W invariant under all of them: either W is all of affine space, or the characteristic is positive and the complement is a finite set of closed points with coordinates algebraic over the prime field (statement lines 7846-7860). The proof is an original argument. It replaces k by an extension and assumes a component Z of the complement of positive dimension, then produces a point with at least one transcendental coordinate and claims that its orbit under the group generated by the transformations is Zariski dense (proof lines 7863-7872). The claim is verified by splitting on the characteristic: in characteristic zero the translation operators alone move the point onto all lattice translates, and in characteristic p one uses the operators T_{i,n,d} to add polynomial functions of a transcendental coordinate, showing the closure contains a coordinate hyperplane and then, repeating with another coordinate, contains infinitely many such translates, which gives density (proof lines 7874-7895). The dimension zero case is then disposed of by the same argument (proof lines 7897-7900). The claim is H3: the construction of the dense orbit with its careful characteristic splitting is genuine independent mathematics.
